summary: Return the prefix sums runningSum[i] = sum(nums[0..i]).
mainInsight: Each prefix sum extends the previous one: out[i] = out[i - 1] + nums[i]. It can be done in place or with itertools.accumulate.

approaches.name: Running total
approaches.summary: Add the current value to the previous prefix.

commonMistakes: Starting the loop at 0 and reading nums[-1]
Using a new list when asked to do it in place

promptVariants: What recurrence defines a running sum?
How do you get each prefix sum from the previous one?
cards.explanation: Each prefix extends the previous one by a single element.

promptVariants: Why is a prefix-sum array useful beyond this problem?
How does it answer range-sum queries?
cards.answer: With prefix sums, the sum of any range [l, r] is pref[r] - pref[l - 1] (or pref[r + 1] - pref[l] with a leading 0), so each query takes O(1) after an O(n) build. Many subarray problems (contiguous array, subarray sum equals k) rely on this.
keyPoints: Range sum = difference of two prefixes
cards.explanation: Combine with a hash map for 'sum equals k' problems.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: The result can overwrite the input (or O(n) for a new list).
